Take each partial derivative, holding the other two variables constant:
$f_x = {a2}xy {c:signedcoef}z$, $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}z^2$, $f_z = {b2}yz {c:signedcoef}x$.
**$\nabla f = \langle {a2}xy {c:signedcoef}z,\; {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}z^2,\; {b2}yz {c:signedcoef}x\rangle$**.

drills.title: Directional derivative
drills.prompt: Find the directional derivative of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2$ at $({x0}, {y0})$ in the direction of $\mathbf v = \langle {v1}, {v2}\rangle$. (2 decimals.)

figure.caption: The direction of v from the point

drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \langle 2({a})x + ({b})y,\; ({b})x + 2({c})y\rangle = \langle {gx}, {gy}\rangle$ at $({x0}, {y0})$.
Normalize: $|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{({v1})^2 + ({v2})^2} \approx {nv:num4}$.
$D_{\mathbf u}f = \dfrac{\nabla f\cdot\mathbf v}{|\mathbf v|} = \dfrac{({gx})({v1}) + ({gy})({v2})}{{nv:num4}} \approx$ **{D:num2}**.

drills.title: Steepest ascent
drills.prompt: For $f(x, y) = {a:coef}xy^2 {b:signedcoef}x^2$ at $({x0}, {y0})$, find the gradient and the maximum rate of increase. (Rate to 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$f_x = {a:coef}y^2 + 2({b})x = {gx}$ and $f_y = 2({a})xy = {gy}$ at the point, so $
abla f = \langle {gx}, {gy}angle$.
The maximum rate of increase is $|
abla f| = \sqrt{({gx})^2 + ({gy})^2} \approx$ **{rate:num2}**, in the direction of $
abla f$.

drills.title: Critical point of a quadratic
drills.prompt: Find the critical point of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2 {d:signedcoef}x {e:signedcoef}y$.
drills.solution:
Set both partials to zero:
$f_x = {a2}x {b:signedcoef}y {d:signed} = 0$ and $f_y = {b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y {e:signed} = 0$.
Solving this linear system (for example by elimination) gives **$x = {p}$, $y = {q}$**. Check: ${a2}({p}) + ({b})({q}) + ({d}) = 0$. ✓

drills.title: Classify a critical point
drills.prompt: The point $({x0}, {y0})$ is a critical point of $f(x, y) = x^3 - {k3}x {c:signedcoef}y^2 {dd:signedcoef}y$. Find the discriminant $D$ there, and classify the point: type **1** for a local minimum, **2** for a local maximum, **3** for a saddle point.
drills.solution:
$f_{xx} = 6x = {fxx}$, $f_{yy} = {fyy}$, $f_{xy} = 0$ at $({x0}, {y0})$.
$D = f_{xx}f_{yy} - f_{xy}^2 = ({fxx})({fyy}) - 0 =$ **{D}**.
If $D < 0$ the point is a saddle; if $D > 0$, the sign of $f_{xx}$ decides (positive: minimum, negative: maximum). Answer: **type {cls}**.

drills.title: Absolute extrema on a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the absolute maximum and minimum of $f(x, y) = (x {np:signed})^2 + (y {nq:signed})^2$ on the rectangle $0 \le x \le {A}$, $0 \le y \le {B}$.

figure.caption: f is the squared distance from ({p}, {q})

drills.solution:
$f$ is the squared distance from $({p}, {q})$. The only critical point is $({p}, {q})$ itself ($\nabla f = \mathbf 0$ there); it counts only if it lies in the rectangle.
Minimum: the closest point of the rectangle is $({p}, {q})$ if it is inside, otherwise the nearest boundary point; this gives **{fmin}**.
Maximum: on each edge $f$ is a parabola in one variable, so the largest value occurs at a corner. The farthest corner gives **{fmax}**.

drills.title: Closest point on a line (Lagrange)
drills.prompt: Use Lagrange multipliers to minimize $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2$ subject to ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {k}$. Give the point and the minimum value. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g$: $2x = {a:coef}\lambda$ and $2y = {b:coef}\lambda$, so $x = \tfrac{{a}}{2}\lambda$, $y = \tfrac{{b}}{2}\lambda$.
Substitute into the constraint: $\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\left(({a})^2 + ({b})^2\right) = {k}$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{2\cdot{k}}{{ss}}$.
Then $x =$ **${X:texfrac}$**, $y =$ **${Y:texfrac}$**, and $f = x^2 + y^2 =$ **${fmin:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Maximize a product (Lagrange)
drills.prompt: Use Lagrange multipliers to maximize $V = xyz$ for $x, y, z > 0$ subject to ${a:coef}x + {b:coef}y + {c:coef}z = {k}$.
drills.solution:
$\nabla V = \lambda\nabla g$: $yz = {a:coef}\lambda$, $xz = {b:coef}\lambda$, $xy = {c:coef}\lambda$.
Multiply by $x$, $y$, $z$ respectively: $xyz = {a:coef}\lambda x = {b:coef}\lambda y = {c:coef}\lambda z$, so ${a:coef}x = {b:coef}y = {c:coef}z$. Each term is one third of {k}.
So ${a:coef}x = {b:coef}y = {c:coef}z = \tfrac{{k}}{3}$: **$x = {X}$, $y = {Y}$, $z = {Z}$**, and $V =$ **{V}**.

drills.title: Least squares line through four points
drills.prompt: Find the least squares line $y = mx + b$ for the points $({xa}, {y1})$, $({xb}, {y2})$, $({xc}, {y3})$, $({xd}, {y4})$. (Exact fractions, or decimals to 2 places.)
drills.solution:
Sums: $n = 4$, $\sum x_i = {sx}$, $\sum y_i = {sy}$, $\sum x_i^2 = {sxx}$, $\sum x_iy_i = {sxy}$.
Normal equations: ${sxx}m + {sx}b = {sxy}$ and ${sx}m + 4b = {sy}$.
Solving: $m = \dfrac{4({sxy}) - ({sx})({sy})}{4({sxx}) - {sx}^2} = \dfrac{{numm}}{{den}} =$ **{m:num4}**.
Then $b = \dfrac{\sum y_i - m\sum x_i}{4} = \dfrac{{sy} - ({m:num4})({sx})}{4} =$ **{b:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve the normal equations from data sums
drills.prompt: A data set of $n = {n}$ points has $\sum x_i = {sx}$, $\sum y_i = {sy}$, $\sum x_i^2 = {sxx}$ and $\sum x_iy_i = {sxy}$. Find the slope $m$ and intercept $b$ of the least squares line $y = mx + b$.
drills.solution:
The normal equations are $m\sum x_i^2 + b\sum x_i = \sum x_iy_i$ and $m\sum x_i + nb = \sum y_i$:
$${sxx}m + {sx}b = {sxy},\qquad {sx}m + {n}b = {sy}.$$
Eliminate $b$: $m = \dfrac{n\sum x_iy_i - \sum x_i\sum y_i}{n\sum x_i^2 - (\sum x_i)^2} = \dfrac{{n}({sxy}) - ({sx})({sy})}{{n}({sxx}) - {sx}^2} = \dfrac{{numm}}{{den}} =$ **{m}**.
Then $b = \left(\sum y_i - m\sum x_i\right)/n = \dfrac{{sy} - ({m})({sx})}{{n}} =$ **{b}**.

drills.title: Best line through the origin
drills.prompt: Fit the model $y = kx$, a line through the origin, to the points $({x1}, {y1})$, $({x2}, {y2})$, $({x3}, {y3})$ by least squares. (Exact fraction, or 3 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Minimize $S(k) = \sum(y_i - kx_i)^2$. Setting $S'(k) = -2\sum x_i(y_i - kx_i) = 0$ gives $k = \dfrac{\sum x_iy_i}{\sum x_i^2}$.
$\sum x_iy_i = {x1}({y1}) + {x2}({y2}) + {x3}({y3}) = {sxy}$ and $\sum x_i^2 = {x1}^2 + {x2}^2 + {x3}^2 = {sxx}$.
So $k = \dfrac{{sxy}}{{sxx}} \approx$ **{k:dp3}**. ($S''(k) = 2\sum x_i^2 > 0$, so this is the minimum.)

drills.title: Double integral over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_R ({p:coef}x + {q:coef}xy)\,dA$ over $R = [{a}, {b}]\times[{c}, {d}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Integrate in $y$ first, holding $x$ constant: $\displaystyle\int_{{c}}^{{d}}({p:coef}x + {q:coef}xy)\,dy = \left[{p:coef}xy + {q:coef}x\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_{y={c}}^{y={d}} = ({p}\cdot{h} + {q}\cdot{Y2})x$.
Then in $x$: $\displaystyle\int_{{a}}^{{b}}x\,dx = \frac{{b}^2 - {a}^2}{2} = {X2}$, so the value is $\left({p}\cdot{h} + {q}\cdot{Y2}\right)({X2}) =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Average value over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the average value of $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2$ over the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\displaystyle\iint_R(x^2 + y^2)\,dA = \int_0^{{B}}\int_0^{{A}}(x^2 + y^2)\,dx\,dy = {B}\cdot\frac{{A}^3}{3} + {A}\cdot\frac{{B}^3}{3} \approx {I:num2}$.
The area is ${A}\cdot{B}$, so $f_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{{A}^2 + {B}^2}{3} \approx$ **{fav:num2}**.

drills.title: Integral over the region between a line and a parabola
drills.prompt: Let $D$ be the region between $y = x^2$ and $y = {m:coef}x$. Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_D({p} {q:signedcoef}x)\,dA$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)

figure.caption: D lies between the parabola and the line for 0 ≤ x ≤ {m}

drills.solution:
The curves meet at $x = 0$ and $x = {m}$, with the line on top. Type I:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{{m}}\int_{x^2}^{{m:coef}x}({p} {q:signedcoef}x)\,dy\,dx = \int_0^{{m}}({p} {q:signedcoef}x)({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx$.
Since $\int_0^{{m}}({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{{m}^3}{6}$ and $\int_0^{{m}}x({m:coef}x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{{m}^4}{12}$, the value is ${p}\cdot\frac{{m}^3}{6} + ({q})\cdot\frac{{m}^4}{12} =$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Reverse the order of integration
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{top}}\int_{x/{k}}^{{b}}e^{y^2}\,dy\,dx$ by reversing the order of integration. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\int e^{y^2}\,dy$ is not elementary, so reverse. The region $0 \le x \le {top}$, $x/{k} \le y \le {b}$ is the triangle $0 \le y \le {b}$, $0 \le x \le {k}y$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\int_0^{{k}y}e^{y^2}\,dx\,dy = \int_0^{{b}}{k}y\,e^{y^2}\,dy = \frac{{k}}{2}\left(e^{{b}^2} - 1\right) \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume under a paraboloid (polar)
drills.prompt: Find the volume of the solid under $z = {H} - {k:coef}(x^2 + y^2)$ and above the $xy$-plane. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
The paraboloid meets $z = 0$ where ${k:coef}r^2 = {H}$, that is $r^2 = {R2:texfrac}$, so the base is the disk $r \le \sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}$.
$V = \displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}}({H} - {k:coef}r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\left[\frac{{H}r^2}{2} - \frac{{k:coef}r^4}{4}\right]_0^{\sqrt{{R2:texfrac}}} = \frac{\pi\cdot{H}^2}{{k2}} \approx$ **{V:num2}**.

drills.title: Area of a rose petal
drills.prompt: Find the area of one petal of the rose $r = {a:coef}\cos({n}\theta)$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
One petal runs between consecutive zeros of $\cos({n}\theta)$: $-\frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}} \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}}$.
Area $= \displaystyle\int_{-\pi/(2\cdot{n})}^{\pi/(2\cdot{n})}\int_0^{{a:coef}\cos({n}\theta)}r\,dr\,d\theta = \frac{{a}^2}{2}\int_{-\pi/(2\cdot{n})}^{\pi/(2\cdot{n})}\cos^2({n}\theta)\,d\theta = \frac{{a}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2\cdot{n}} \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Mass of a lamina
drills.prompt: A lamina occupies $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$ and has density $\rho(x, y) = {p} + {q:coef}x + {s:coef}y$. Find its mass. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution: $m = \displaystyle\int_0^{{A}}\int_0^{{B}}({p} + {q:coef}x + {s:coef}y)\,dy\,dx = {p}({A})({B}) + {q}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B} + {s}\cdot{A}\cdot\frac{{B}^2}{2} =$ **{m:num2}**.

drills.title: Centroid of the region under a power curve
drills.prompt: Find the centroid of the region under $y = {k:coef}{n}$ for $0 \le x \le {a}$ (above the $x$-axis). (2 decimals.)

figure.caption: The region under the curve for 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}

drills.solution:
Area $A = \displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}{k:coef}{n}\,dx \approx {area:num4}$.
$\bar x = \dfrac1A\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}x\cdot {k:coef}{n}\,dx$ and $\bar y = \dfrac1A\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{k:coef}{n}}y\,dy\,dx = \dfrac1A\int_0^{{a}}\frac{({k:coef}{n})^2}{2}\,dx$.
These give **$\bar x \approx {xb:num2}$** and **$\bar y \approx {yb:num2}$**.

drills.title: Surface area of a plane over a rectangle
drills.prompt: Find the area of the part of the plane $z = {c} {p:signedcoef}x {q:signedcoef}y$ that lies above the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$f_x = {p}$ and $f_y = {q}$, so the stretch factor is $\sqrt{1 + ({p})^2 + ({q})^2} \approx {fac:num4}$, constant.
Area $= \displaystyle\iint_R\sqrt{1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2}\,dA = {A}\cdot{B}\cdot{fac:num4} \approx$ **{S:num2}**.

drills.title: A joint density on a rectangle
drills.prompt: The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint density $f(x, y) = Cxy$ on the rectangle $0 \le x \le {a}$, $0 \le y \le {bb}$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find the constant $C$, the probability $P(X \le {s},\ Y \le {t})$, and the mean $E(X)$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
Total probability 1: $\displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{bb}}Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{a2}}{2}\cdot\frac{{b2}}{2} = 1$, so $C =$ **${cc:texfrac}$**.
$P = \displaystyle\int_0^{{s}}\int_0^{{t}}Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{s}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{t}^2}{2} =$ **${prob:texfrac}$**.
$E(X) = \displaystyle\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{bb}}x\cdot Cxy\,dy\,dx = C\cdot\frac{{a}^3}{3}\cdot\frac{{b2}}{2} =$ **${ex:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Triple integral over a box
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_B({p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}yz)\,dV$ over the box $B = [0, {a}]\times[0, {b}]\times[0, {c}]$. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Split and factor each term over the box:
$\displaystyle\iiint {p:coef}x\,dV = {p}\cdot\frac{{a}^2}{2}\cdot{b}\cdot{c} = {t1}$ and $\displaystyle\iiint {q:coef}yz\,dV = ({q})\cdot{a}\cdot\frac{{b}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{c}^2}{2} = {t2}$.
Total: **{ans}**.

drills.title: Volume and centroid height of a tetrahedron
drills.prompt: The tetrahedron $E$ is bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane $\dfrac{x}{{a}} + \dfrac{y}{{b}} + \dfrac{z}{{c}} = 1$. Find its volume and the $z$-coordinate of its centroid. (Exact or 2 decimals.)

figure.caption: Shadow on the xy-plane: 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}, 0 ≤ y ≤ {b}(1 − x/{a})

drills.solution:
Top surface $z = {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)$ over the triangle with legs {a} and {b}.
$V = \displaystyle\iint_D {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)dA = \frac{{a}\cdot{b}\cdot{c}}{6} =$ **{V:num2}**.
Likewise $\iiint_E z\,dV = \dfrac{{a}\cdot{b}\cdot{c}^2}{24}$, so $\bar z = \dfrac{{c}}{4} =$ **{zb:num2}** (the average of the vertices' heights).

drills.title: Rectangular to cylindrical
drills.prompt: Convert $({x}, {y}, {z})$ to cylindrical coordinates $(r, \theta, z)$ with $0 \le \theta < 2\pi$ ($\theta$ in radians, 2 decimals).
drills.solution:
$r = \sqrt{({x})^2 + ({y})^2} \approx {r:num2}$.
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{{y}}{{x}}$; checking the quadrant of $({x}, {y})$ gives $\theta \approx {th:num2}$ rad (about {thd:num1}°).
$z$ is unchanged. So **$(r, \theta, z) \approx ({r:num2},\ {th:num2},\ {z})$**.

drills.title: Integral over a cylinder
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_E(x^2 + y^2 {c:signedcoef}z)\,dV$, where $E$ is the solid cylinder $x^2 + y^2 \le {a}^2$, $0 \le z \le {h}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
In cylindrical coordinates the integrand is $r^2 {c:signedcoef}z$ and $dV = r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{{a}}\int_0^{{h}}(r^2 {c:signedcoef}z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\left[{h}\cdot\frac{{a}^4}{4} + {c}\cdot\frac{{h}^2}{2}\cdot\frac{{a}^2}{2}\right] \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Spherical to rectangular
drills.prompt: Convert the spherical point $\rho = {rho}$, $\theta = {thd}^\circ$, $\phi = {phd}^\circ$ to rectangular coordinates. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$x = \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta = {rho}\sin{phd}^\circ\cos{thd}^\circ \approx {X:num2}$,
$y = \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta = {rho}\sin{phd}^\circ\sin{thd}^\circ \approx {Y:num2}$,
$z = \rho\cos\phi = {rho}\cos{phd}^\circ \approx {Z:num2}$.
**$(x, y, z) \approx ({X:num2}, {Y:num2}, {Z:num2})$**.

drills.title: Radial integral over a ball
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iiint_B {n}\,dV$ over the ball $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \le {a}^2$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
In spherical coordinates $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2} = \rho$, so the integrand is a power of $\rho$; multiplied by the $\rho^2$ in $dV = \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\theta\,d\phi$ it becomes $\rho^{{n2}}$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\sin\phi\,d\phi\int_0^{2\pi}d\theta\int_0^{{a}}\rho^{{n2}}\,d\rho = 2\cdot2\pi\cdot\frac{{a}^{{n3}}}{{n3}} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Compute a Jacobian
drills.prompt: Find the Jacobian $\dfrac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)}$ for $x = {a:coef}u^2 {b:signedcoef}v$, $y = {c:coef}uv$.
drills.solution:
$x_u = {a2}u$, $x_v = {b}$, $y_u = {c:coef}v$, $y_v = {c:coef}u$.
$\dfrac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} = x_uy_v - x_vy_u = ({a2}u)({c:coef}u) - ({b})({c:coef}v) =$ **${k1}u^2 {k2:signedcoef}v$**.

drills.title: Area of a parallelogram by change of variables
drills.prompt: Let $R$ be the parallelogram bounded by $x {p:signedcoef}y = 0$, $x {p:signedcoef}y = {A}$, ${q:coef}x + y = 0$ and ${q:coef}x + y = {B}$. Using $u = x {p:signedcoef}y$ and $v = {q:coef}x + y$, find the area of $R$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
$\dfrac{\partial(u, v)}{\partial(x, y)} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & {p}\\ {q} & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - ({p})({q}) = {Ju}$, so $\left|\dfrac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right| = \dfrac{1}{|{Ju}|}$.
The new region is the rectangle $0 \le u \le {A}$, $0 \le v \le {B}$, so the area is $\dfrac{{A}\cdot{B}}{|{Ju}|} =$ **${area:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Evaluate a vector field
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf F(x, y) = \langle {a:coef}xy {b:signed},\; {c:coef}x^2 - y\rangle$, find $\mathbf F({x0}, {y0})$.

figure.caption: The field F, with the point marked

drills.solution:
Substitute $x = {x0}$, $y = {y0}$ into each component:
$P = ({a})({x0})({y0}) + ({b}) = {P0}$ and $Q = ({c})({x0})^2 - ({y0}) = {Q0}$.
**$\mathbf F({x0}, {y0}) = \langle {P0}, {Q0}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Gradient field
drills.prompt: Find the gradient field of $f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}y^3 {c:signedcoef}x$.
drills.solution:
$\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y\rangle$ with $f_x = {a2}xy {c:signed}$ and $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b3:signedcoef}y^2$.
**$\nabla f = \langle {a2}xy {c:signed},\; {a:coef}x^2 {b3:signedcoef}y^2\rangle$**.

drills.title: Scalar line integral along a segment
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_C({p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}y)\,ds$, where $C$ is the segment from $({x1}, {y1})$ to $({x2}, {y2})$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {x1} + ({dx})t,\; {y1} + ({dy})t\rangle$, $0 \le t \le 1$, so $|\mathbf r'(t)| = \sqrt{({dx})^2 + ({dy})^2} \approx {L:num4}$.
The integrand is linear in $t$, so $\int_0^1 f(\mathbf r(t))\,dt$ is its value at the midpoint $({mx}, {my})$: ${p}({mx}) + ({q})({my}) = {avgf}$.
Value $= {avgf}\cdot{L:num4} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Work along a power curve
drills.prompt: Find the work done by $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2,\; {b:coef}xy\rangle$ on a particle moving along $y = x^{n}$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(1, 1)$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t, t^{n}\rangle$, $0 \le t \le 1$, so $\mathbf r'(t) = \langle 1, {n}t^{{n} - 1}\rangle$ and $\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t)) = \langle {a:coef}t^2,\; {b:coef}t^{{n1}}\rangle$.
$\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf r' = {a:coef}t^2 + ({b})({n})\,t^{{nn}}$, so $W = \displaystyle\int_0^1\left({a:coef}t^2 + ({b})({n})\,t^{{nn}}\right)dt = \frac{{a}}{3} + \frac{{b}\cdot{n}}{{n2}} =$ **${W:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Find a potential function
drills.prompt: The field $\mathbf F = \langle {a2}x {b:signedcoef}y {d:signed},\; {b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y\rangle$ is conservative. Find a potential function $f(x, y)$.
drills.solution:
Check: $P_y = {b} = Q_x$. ✓ Integrate $P$ in $x$: $f = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {d:signedcoef}x + g(y)$.
Then $f_y = {b:coef}x + g'(y)$ must equal ${b:coef}x {c2:signedcoef}y$, so $g'(y) = {c2}y$ and $g = {c:coef}y^2$.
**$f(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2 {d:signedcoef}x$** (plus any constant).

drills.title: Fundamental theorem for line integrals
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a2}xy,\; {a:coef}x^2 {b:signed}\rangle$, where $C$ is any path from $({x1}, {y1})$ to $({x2}, {y2})$.
drills.solution:
$P_y = {a2}x = Q_x$, so $\mathbf F$ is conservative, with potential $f = {a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}y$ (check: $f_x = {a2}xy$, $f_y = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signed}$).
By the fundamental theorem: $f({x2}, {y2}) - f({x1}, {y1}) = {fB} - ({fA}) =$ **{W}**.

drills.title: Green's theorem on a rectangle
drills.prompt: Use Green's theorem to evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_C {a:coef}xy\,dx + ({b:coef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x)\,dy$, where $C$ is the boundary of the rectangle $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]$, counterclockwise.
drills.solution:
$Q_x - P_y = ({b2}x {c:signed}) - ({a:coef}x) = {k:coef}x {c:signed}$.
$\displaystyle\iint_R({k:coef}x {c:signed})\,dA = {k}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B} + ({c})\cdot{A}\cdot{B} =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Area of a triangle with Green's theorem
drills.prompt: Use $A = \tfrac12\oint_C x\,dy - y\,dx$ to find the area of the triangle with vertices $O(0, 0)$, $P({x1}, {y1})$, $Q({x2}, {y2})$ (traversed $O \to P \to Q \to O$, which is counterclockwise).
drills.solution:
On a segment from $(x_a, y_a)$ to $(x_b, y_b)$, $\int x\,dy - y\,dx = x_ay_b - x_by_a$. The two sides through $O$ contribute 0.
The side $P \to Q$ contributes $({x1})({y2}) - ({x2})({y1}) = {cr}$.
$A = \tfrac12\cdot{cr} =$ **{area}**.

drills.title: Compute a curl
drills.prompt: Find $\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}xy {p:signedcoef}z,\; {b:coef}yz,\; {c:coef}xz\rangle$.
drills.solution:
With $P = {a:coef}xy {p:signedcoef}z$, $Q = {b:coef}yz$, $R = {c:coef}xz$:
$\mathbf i$: $R_y - Q_z = 0 - ({b})y$; $\mathbf j$: $P_z - R_x = {p} - ({c})z$; $\mathbf k$: $Q_x - P_y = 0 - ({a})x$.
**$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F = \langle {nb:coef}y,\; {p} {nc:signedcoef}z,\; {na:coef}x\rangle$**.

drills.title: Compute a divergence
drills.prompt: Find $\operatorname{div}\mathbf F$ for $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2y,\; {b:coef}yz^2,\; {c:coef}xz\rangle$.
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = P_x + Q_y + R_z = {a2}xy + ({b})z^2 + ({c})x$.
**$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a2}xy {b:signedcoef}z^2 {c:signedcoef}x$**.

drills.title: Normal vector to a parametric surface
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf r(u, v) = \langle u + v,\; {a:coef}u^2,\; {b:coef}v^2\rangle$, find the normal vector $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$ at $u = {u0}$, $v = {v0}$.
drills.solution:
$\mathbf r_u = \langle 1,\; 2({a})u,\; 0\rangle = \langle 1, {ru2}, 0\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_v = \langle 1,\; 0,\; 2({b})v\rangle = \langle 1, 0, {rv3}\rangle$ at the point.
$\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v = \langle ({ru2})({rv3}) - 0,\; 0 - (1)({rv3}),\; 0 - ({ru2})(1)\rangle =$ **$\langle {N1}, {N2}, {N3}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Surface area of a cone
drills.prompt: Find the area of the cone $z = {k:coef}\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ between $z = 0$ and $z = {h}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize $\mathbf r(r, \theta) = \langle r\cos\theta,\; r\sin\theta,\; {k:coef}r\rangle$ with $0 \le r \le {R}$ (since $z = {h}$ when $r = {R}$), $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$.
$\mathbf r_r\times\mathbf r_\theta = \langle -{k:coef}r\cos\theta,\; -{k:coef}r\sin\theta,\; r\rangle$, of length $r\sqrt{1 + {k}^2}$.
$A = \displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{{R}}r\sqrt{1 + {k}^2}\,dr\,d\theta = \pi\cdot{R}^2\sqrt{1 + {k}^2} \approx$ **{A:num2}**.

drills.title: Flux through a slanted triangle
drills.prompt: Find the flux of $\mathbf F = \langle x, y, z\rangle$ upward through the part of the plane $\dfrac{x}{{a}} + \dfrac{y}{{b}} + \dfrac{z}{{c}} = 1$ in the first octant. (Exact or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Write the plane as $z = g(x, y) = {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right)$, so $g_x = -\frac{{c}}{{a}}$ and $g_y = -\frac{{c}}{{b}}$.
Upward flux integrand: $-Pg_x - Qg_y + R = \frac{{c}}{{a}}x + \frac{{c}}{{b}}y + {c}\left(1 - \frac{x}{{a}} - \frac{y}{{b}}\right) = {c}$, a constant.
The shadow is a right triangle with legs {a} and {b}, area $\frac{{a}\cdot{b}}{2}$, so the flux is ${c}\cdot\frac{{a}\cdot{b}}{2} =$ **{flux}**.

drills.title: Surface integral over a hemisphere
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_S({p} + {q:coef}z)\,dS$, where $S$ is the upper hemisphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = {a}^2$, $z \ge 0$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Parametrize with spherical angles: $z = {a}\cos\phi$ and $dS = {a}^2\sin\phi\,d\phi\,d\theta$ for $0 \le \phi \le \frac\pi2$.
$\iint_S {p}\,dS = {p}\cdot2\pi\cdot{a}^2 \approx {t1:num2}$ (the area of the hemisphere is $2\pi a^2$), and $\iint_S {q:coef}z\,dS = {q}\cdot\pi\cdot{a}^3 \approx {t2:num2}$.
Total $\approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Circulation by Stokes' theorem
drills.prompt: Use Stokes' theorem to evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for $\mathbf F = \langle -{a:coef}y^3,\; {b:coef}x^3,\; z\rangle$, where $C$ is the circle $x^2 + y^2 = {R}^2$ in the plane $z = {h}$, counterclockwise seen from above. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F = \langle 0,\; 0,\; 3({b})x^2 + 3({a})y^2\rangle$. Use the flat disk at height {h} with $\mathbf n = \mathbf k$.
Over a disk of radius $R$, $\iint x^2\,dA = \iint y^2\,dA = \frac{\pi R^4}{4}$, so the flux of the curl is $3({b} + {a})\cdot\frac{\pi\cdot{R}^4}{4} \approx$ **{ans:num2}**. (The height {h} does not matter.)

drills.title: Divergence theorem on a box
drills.prompt: Use the Divergence theorem to find the outward flux of $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2,\; {b:coef}y^2,\; {c:coef}z^2\rangle$ through the surface of the box $[0, {A}]\times[0, {B}]\times[0, {C}]$.
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a2}x + ({b2})y + ({c2})z$.
$\displaystyle\iiint {a2}x\,dV = {a2}\cdot\frac{{A}^2}{2}\cdot{B}\cdot{C}$, and similarly for the other terms. Adding:
${a}\cdot{A}^2\cdot{B}\cdot{C} + ({b})\cdot{A}\cdot{B}^2\cdot{C} + ({c})\cdot{A}\cdot{B}\cdot{C}^2 =$ **{ans}**.

drills.title: Divergence theorem on a ball
drills.prompt: Find the outward flux of $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x + y^2,\; {b:coef}y + z^2,\; {c:coef}z + x^2\rangle$ through the sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = {R}^2$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a} {b:signed} {c:signed} = {d}$ (the squared terms have zero partial derivatives in their own slots).
By the Divergence theorem the flux is ${d}\cdot\frac43\pi\cdot{R}^3 \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Gauss's law
drills.prompt: A point charge of {qn} nC sits inside a closed surface (a sphere of radius {r} cm around it). Using $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N·m}^2)$, find the electric flux through the surface in N·m²/C (3 significant figures).
drills.solution: By Gauss's law the flux is $Q_{\text{enc}}/\varepsilon_0$, whatever the radius: $\dfrac{{qn}\times10^{-9}}{8.854\times10^{-12}} \approx$ **{flux:sig3}** N·m²/C.

drills.title: Gravity inside and outside a uniform planet
drills.prompt: A planet is modeled as a uniform ball of radius {Rkm} km with surface gravity {gs} m/s². Find the field strength $|\mathbf g|$ (a) {dep} km below the surface and (b) {ht} km above the surface. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: Only the mass closer to the center counts. Inside a uniform ball the enclosed mass grows like $r^3$, so $|\mathbf g| = g_0\,r/R$: at $r = {rin:dp0}$ km, $|\mathbf g| = {gs}\cdot\dfrac{{rin:dp0}}{{Rkm:dp0}} =$ **{gin:sig3}** m/s². Outside, the planet acts like a point mass, so $|\mathbf g| = g_0R^2/r^2$: at $r = {rout:dp0}$ km, $|\mathbf g| = {gs}\cdot\left(\dfrac{{Rkm:dp0}}{{rout:dp0}}\right)^2 =$ **{gout:sig3}** m/s².

drills.title: A tunnel through a uniform planet
drills.prompt: A uniform planet has radius {Rkm} km and surface gravity {gs} m/s². A stone is dropped into a straight frictionless tunnel through the center. How many minutes does it take to reach the far side? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: Inside, the force per kilogram along the tunnel is $-\dfrac{g_0}{R}x$, so $x'' = -\dfrac{g_0}{R}x$: simple harmonic motion with period $T = 2\pi\sqrt{R/g_0} = 2\pi\sqrt{{Rm:dp0}/{gs}} \approx {per:sig3}$ s. The far side is half a period away: $T/2 = {per:sig3}/2$ s $=$ **{oneway:sig3}** minutes.

drills.title: Density from the potential (Poisson's equation)
drills.prompt: Inside a body the gravitational potential is $\Phi = ({kk}\times10^{-7}\text{ s}^{-2})(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) + C$ (in J/kg, lengths in meters). Use Poisson's equation with $G = 6.674\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² to find the density, in kg/m³, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$
abla^2(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6$, so $
abla^2\Phi = {lap}	imes10^{-7}$ s⁻². Poisson: $ho = \dfrac{
abla^2\Phi}{4\pi G} = \dfrac{{lap}	imes10^{-7}}{4\pi(6.674	imes10^{-11})} =$ **{rho:sig3}** kg/m³.

drills.title: The curl of a curl
drills.prompt: Let $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x^2y,\ {b:coef}yz^2,\ {c:coef}x^2z\rangle$. Find $\nabla\times(\nabla\times\mathbf F)$ at the point $({p}, {q}, {w})$.
drills.solution:
Use $
abla	imes(
abla	imes\mathbf F) = 
abla(
abla\cdot\mathbf F) - 
abla^2\mathbf F$. Here $
abla\cdot\mathbf F = {ta}xy + ({b})z^2 + ({c})x^2$, so $
abla(
abla\cdot\mathbf F) = \langle {ta}y + ({tc})x,\ {ta}x,\ {tb}zangle$, which is $\langle {gx}, {gy}, {gz}angle$ at the point. Componentwise Laplacians: $
abla^2\mathbf F = \langle {ta}y,\ {tb}y,\ {tc}zangle = \langle {lx}, {ly}, {lz}angle$ there. Subtract: **{c1}**, **{c2}**, **{c3}**.

drills.title: Field amplitudes from intensity
drills.prompt: A plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum has intensity {inten} W/m². Using $c = 2.998\times10^8$ m/s and $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}$ F/m, find the amplitude $E_0$ of the electric field (V/m) and $B_0$ of the magnetic field (in microtesla, μT). Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $I = \tfrac12c\varepsilon_0E_0^2$, so $E_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2({inten:dp0})}{(2.998\times10^8)(8.854\times10^{-12})}} =$ **{e0:sig3}** V/m. Then $B_0 = E_0/c = {e0:sig3}/(2.998\times10^8)$ T $=$ **{b0:sig3}** μT.

drills.title: Averages of a harmonic function
drills.prompt: Let $u = {a:coef}x^2 {na:signedcoef}y^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}x$. Find the average value of $u$ over the circle of radius {rad} centered at $({p}, {q})$.
drills.solution: $u_{xx} + u_{yy} = {ta} + ({nta}) = 0$, so $u$ is harmonic. By the mean value property its average over any circle equals its value at the center, whatever the radius: $u({p}, {q}) =$ **{val}**.

drills.title: Making a quadratic harmonic
drills.prompt: (a) Find the constant $k$ that makes $u = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}y^2 + kz^2$ harmonic. (b) With that $k$, find the average of $u$ over the sphere of radius 2 centered at $({p}, {q}, {w})$.
drills.solution: $\nabla^2u = {ta} + ({tb}) + 2k = 0$ gives $k =$ **{cc}**. Then $u$ is harmonic, so its average over a sphere is its value at the center: ${a}({p})^2 + ({b})({q})^2 + ({cc})({w})^2 =$ **{val}**.

drills.title: Potential flow past a cylinder
drills.prompt: Water flows at speed {U} m/s past a long cylinder of radius {rad} m, with potential $\phi = {U}\left(r + \dfrac{a^2}{r}\right)\cos\theta$ ($a = {rad}$). Find the speed (a) on the cylinder at $\theta = {ang}^\circ$ and (b) on the axis directly upstream, at distance {dist} m from the center. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: On the wall the velocity is tangential: $\dfrac1r\dfrac{\partial\phi}{\partial\theta} = -2U\sin\theta$, so the speed is $2({U})|\sin {ang}^\circ| =$ **{wall:sig3}** m/s. On the upstream axis ($\theta = \pi$) the velocity is radial, and here $r/a = {mult}$: $\left|\dfrac{\partial\phi}{\partial r}\right| = U\left(1 - \dfrac{a^2}{r^2}\right) = {U}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{mult}^2}\right) =$ **{ahead:sig3}** m/s, slowing toward the stagnation point at $r = a$.

drills.title: Principal and Gaussian curvature at a flat spot
drills.prompt: For the surface $z = {p:coef}x^2 {q:signedcoef}xy {s:signedcoef}y^2$ at the origin (normal $\mathbf k$), find the principal curvatures $\kappa_1 \ge \kappa_2$ (2 decimal places) and the Gaussian curvature $K$.
drills.solution: The gradient is zero at the origin, so the principal curvatures are the eigenvalues of the Hessian $\begin{bmatrix}{tp} & {q}\\ {q} & {ts}\end{bmatrix}$. Their sum is the trace ${tr}$ and their product the determinant ${kg}$, so $\lambda = {ps} \pm\sqrt{({pms})^2 + ({q})^2}$: $\kappa_1 =$ **{k1:num2}**, $\kappa_2 =$ **{k2:num2}**, and $K = \det = ({tp})({ts}) - ({q})^2 =$ **{kg}**.

drills.title: Gaussian curvature of a paraboloid
drills.prompt: Find the Gaussian curvature of $z = {a:coef}(x^2 + y^2)$ at the point above $({p}, {q})$. Give an exact fraction or 4 significant figures.
drills.solution: $f_{xx} = f_{yy} = {ta}$, $f_{xy} = 0$, $f_x = {fx}$, $f_y = {fy}$. So $K = \dfrac{f_{xx}f_{yy} - f_{xy}^2}{(1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2)^2} = \dfrac{{num:dp0}}{{den:dp0}} \approx$ **{kk:sig4}**.

drills.title: Area of a spherical triangle
drills.prompt: A geodesic triangle on a sphere of radius {Rad} has angles ${A}^\circ$, ${B}^\circ$ and ${C}^\circ$. Find its area (in square units of the radius) to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: By Gauss–Bonnet with $K = 1/R^2$, the angle excess equals area$/R^2$. Excess: ${A} + {B} + {C} - 180 = {exc}^\circ = {exc}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{180}$ rad. Area $= {exc}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{180}\cdot{Rad:dp0}^2 =$ **{area:sig3}**.

drills.title: Distance from a point to a line
drills.prompt: Find the distance from $Q({qx}, {qy}, {qz})$ to the line through $P({px}, {py}, {pz})$ with direction $\mathbf v = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3}\rangle$. (Exact value or 2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
$\overrightarrow{PQ} = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$ and $\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\mathbf v = \langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3}\rangle$, whose length is $\sqrt{{cc}}$. Also $|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{{vv}}$.
Area over base: $D = \dfrac{\sqrt{{cc}}}{\sqrt{{vv}}} \approx$ **{dist:num2}**.

drills.title: Distance between skew lines
drills.prompt: Find the distance between the skew lines $\mathbf r_1 = \langle {ax}, {ay}, {az}\rangle + t\langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3}\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_2 = \langle {bx}, {by}, {bz}\rangle + s\langle {w1}, {w2}, {w3}\rangle$. (Exact value or 2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf n = \mathbf v_1\times\mathbf v_2 = \langle {n1}, {n2}, {n3}\rangle$, with $|\mathbf n| = \sqrt{{nn}}$. $\overrightarrow{P_1P_2} = \langle {d1}, {d2}, {d3}\rangle$ and $\overrightarrow{P_1P_2}\cdot\mathbf n = {trip}$.
Box height: $D = \dfrac{{atrip}}{\sqrt{{nn}}} \approx$ **{dist:num2}**.

drills.title: Vector triple product by BAC−CAB
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf a = \langle {a1}, {a2}, {a3}\rangle$, $\mathbf b = \langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle$, $\mathbf c = \langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3}\rangle$, find $\mathbf a\times(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)$.
drills.solution:
Use $\mathbf a\times(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c) = \mathbf b\,(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c) - \mathbf c\,(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b)$.
$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c = {ac}$ and $\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = {ab}$, so the result is $({ac})\langle {b1}, {b2}, {b3}\rangle - ({ab})\langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3}\rangle =$ **$\langle {r1}, {r2}, {r3}\rangle$**.

drills.title: Eigenvalues of a quadratic form
drills.prompt: Find the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2$. Give the larger one first.
drills.solution:
The matrix is $\begin{bmatrix} {a} & {h}\\ {h} & {c}\end{bmatrix}$ (half of the $xy$ coefficient off the diagonal).
$\lambda = \dfrac{A + C}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{A - C}{2}\right)^2 + h^2} = \dfrac{{tr} \pm \sqrt{({dif})^2 + 4({h})^2}}{2} = \dfrac{{tr} \pm {s}}{2}$,
so $\lambda_1 =$ **{lam1}** and $\lambda_2 =$ **{lam2}**. (Check: their sum is ${tr}$, the sum of the diagonal entries.)

drills.title: Angle that removes the xy term
drills.prompt: Find the angle $\theta$ with $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$ such that rotating the axes by $\theta$ removes the $xy$ term from the quadratic form ${a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}xy {c:signedcoef}y^2$. (Degrees, 1 decimal place.)
drills.solution:
The cross term vanishes when $\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{A - C}{B} = \dfrac{{dif}}{{b}}$.
With $0^\circ < 2\theta < 180^\circ$ this gives $2\theta \approx {twoth:num2}^\circ$, so $\theta \approx$ **{th:num1}°**.

drills.title: Curvature and torsion of a helix
drills.prompt: Find the curvature $\kappa$ and torsion $\tau$ of the helix $\mathbf r(t) = \langle {aa:coef}\cos t,\; {aa:coef}\sin t,\; {bb:coef}t\rangle$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution:
$\mathbf r' = \langle -{aa:coef}\sin t,\; {aa:coef}\cos t,\; {bb}\rangle$, $\mathbf r'' = \langle -{aa:coef}\cos t,\; -{aa:coef}\sin t,\; 0\rangle$, $\mathbf r''' = \langle {aa:coef}\sin t,\; -{aa:coef}\cos t,\; 0\rangle$.
$\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r'' = \langle {ab:coef}\sin t,\; {mab:coef}\cos t,\; {a2}\rangle$, so $|\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''|^2 = {a2}\cdot{den} = {cs:dp0}$ and $(\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r'')\cdot\mathbf r''' = {a2b}$.
$\tau = \dfrac{{a2b}}{{cs:dp0}} =$ **${tau:texfrac}$**, and $\kappa = \dfrac{|\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''|}{|\mathbf r'|^3} = \dfrac{a}{a^2 + b^2} = \dfrac{{aa}}{{den}} =$ **${kap:texfrac}$** (here $a = {aa}$, $b = {bb}$).

drills.title: Torsion of a cubic curve
drills.prompt: Find the torsion of $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t,\; {p:coef}t^2,\; {q:coef}t^3\rangle$ at $t = {t0}$. (Exact fraction, or 3 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
At $t = {t0}$: $\mathbf r' = \langle 1,\; {r1y},\; {r1z}\rangle$, $\mathbf r'' = \langle 0,\; {r2y},\; {r2z}\rangle$, $\mathbf r''' = \langle 0,\; 0,\; {r3z}\rangle$.
$\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r'' = \langle {cx},\; {cy},\; {cz}\rangle$, so $|\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r''|^2 = {nn:dp0}$.
Triple product: $(\mathbf r'\times\mathbf r'')\cdot\mathbf r''' = ({cz})({r3z}) = {trip}$.
$\tau = \dfrac{{trip}}{{nn:dp0}} = {tau:texfrac} \approx$ **{tau:dp3}**.

drills.title: Designing a transition curve
drills.prompt: A clothoid transition of length {Len} m joins a straight track to a circular curve of radius {Rad} m. Trains run at a constant {vel} m/s. Find the total angle the transition turns through (in degrees), the sideways acceleration $v^2/R$ at its end, and the lateral jerk. (Angle and acceleration to 2 decimals, jerk to 3 decimals; ignore cant.)
drills.solution:
The curvature grows linearly from 0 to $1/R$, so the tangent angle is $\theta = \dfrac{L}{2R} = \dfrac{{Len}}{2\cdot{Rad:dp0}} \approx {th:num4}$ rad $\approx$ **{thdeg:num2}°**.
At the end, $a_N = \kappa v^2 = \dfrac{{vel}^2}{{Rad:dp0}} \approx$ **{aN:num2} m/s²**, reached after $L/v \approx {tt:num2}$ s.
Because $a_N$ rises linearly in time, the jerk is $\dfrac{v^3}{RL} = \dfrac{{vel}^3}{{Rad:dp0}\cdot{Len}} \approx$ **{jerk:dp3} m/s³**.

drills.title: Speed and period of a circular orbit
drills.prompt: A satellite is in a circular orbit {alt} km above Earth's surface. Take Earth's radius as 6,371 km and $GM = 3.986\times10^{5}\text{ km}^3/\text{s}^2$. Find its speed (km/s, 2 decimals) and its period (minutes, 1 decimal).
drills.solution:
Distances are from Earth's center: $r = 6{,}371 + {alt:dp0} = {rad:dp0}$ km.
Gravity supplies the centripetal acceleration: $v^2/r = GM/r^2$, so $v = \sqrt{GM/r} = \sqrt{398{,}600/{rad:dp0}} \approx$ **{spd:num2} km/s**.
$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} \approx {secs:dp0}$ s, that is $T \approx$ **{per:num1} minutes**.

drills.title: Orbit size and period from perihelion and aphelion
drills.prompt: A comet orbits the Sun with perihelion distance {peri} AU and aphelion distance {aph} AU. Find the semi-major axis $a$ (AU), the eccentricity $e$ (3 decimals) and the period (years, 2 decimals).
drills.solution:
The semi-major axis is the average of the closest and farthest distances: $a = \dfrac{{peri} + {aph}}{2} =$ **{sma:num2} AU**.
From $r_p = a(1 - e)$ and $r_a = a(1 + e)$: $e = \dfrac{r_a - r_p}{r_a + r_p} = \dfrac{{aph} - {peri}}{{aph} + {peri}} \approx$ **{ecc:dp3}**.
For the Sun in years and AU, Kepler's third law is $T^2 = a^3$, so $T = a^{3/2} \approx$ **{T:num2} years**.

drills.title: A directional derivative from the definition
drills.prompt: Let $f(x, y) = \dfrac{x^2y}{x^2 + y^2}$ with $f(0, 0) = 0$. Using the definition $D_{\mathbf u}f(0,0) = \lim_{t\to0}\dfrac{f(tu_1, tu_2)}{t}$, find the directional derivative at the origin in the direction of $\mathbf v = \langle {p}, {q}\rangle$. (3 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Normalize: $|\mathbf v| = \sqrt{{p2} + {q2}} = \sqrt{{nn}}$, so $\mathbf u = \langle u_1, u_2\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{{nn}}}\langle {p}, {q}\rangle$.
Along the line, $f(tu_1, tu_2) = \dfrac{t^3u_1^2u_2}{t^2(u_1^2 + u_2^2)} = t\,u_1^2u_2$, so $D_{\mathbf u}f(0,0) = u_1^2u_2 = \dfrac{{p2}\cdot({q})}{{nn}\sqrt{{nn}}} \approx$ **{D:dp3}**.
Both partials at the origin are 0, so if $f$ were differentiable this would be $\nabla f\cdot\mathbf u = 0$. It is not 0, which shows again that $f$ is not differentiable at the origin.

drills.title: Unequal mixed partials at the origin
drills.solution:
Since $f(0, y) = 0$, $f_x(0, y) = \lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(h, y)}{h} = \lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{y({p:coef}h^2 - {q:coef}y^2)}{h^2 + y^2} = -{q:coef}y$ (also true at $y = 0$). So $f_{xy}(0,0) = \dfrac{d}{dy}(-{q:coef}y) =$ **{mq}**.
Since $f(x, 0) = 0$, $f_y(x, 0) = \lim_{k\to0}\dfrac{f(x, k)}{k} = \lim_{k\to0}\dfrac{x({p:coef}x^2 - {q:coef}k^2)}{x^2 + k^2} = {p:coef}x$. So $f_{yx}(0,0) =$ **{p}**.
They differ, so the mixed partials cannot be continuous at the origin (Clairaut's theorem would force them to agree).

drills.title: Derivative matrix of a map
drills.prompt: Find the derivative matrix $D\mathbf F({u0}, {v0})$ of $\mathbf F(u, v) = \left({a:coef}u^2v,\ uv {b:signedcoef}v^2\right)$. Enter its entries.
drills.solution:
Row 1 is the gradient of $F_1 = {a:coef}u^2v$ with respect to $(u, v)$: $\langle {a2}uv,\ {a:coef}u^2\rangle$, which at $({u0}, {v0})$ is $\langle {e11}, {e12}\rangle$.
Row 2 is the gradient of $F_2 = uv {b:signedcoef}v^2$: $\langle v,\ u {b2:signedcoef}v\rangle$, which at $({u0}, {v0})$ is $\langle {e21}, {e22}\rangle$.
**$D\mathbf F({u0}, {v0}) = \begin{bmatrix} {e11} & {e12}\\ {e21} & {e22}\end{bmatrix}$**

drills.title: The chain rule as a matrix product
drills.prompt: At a point $\mathbf a$, $D\mathbf F(\mathbf a) = \begin{bmatrix} {a11} & {a12}\\ {a21} & {a22}\end{bmatrix}$, and at $\mathbf F(\mathbf a)$, $D\mathbf G = \begin{bmatrix} {b11} & {b12}\\ {b21} & {b22}\end{bmatrix}$. Find $D(\mathbf G\circ\mathbf F)(\mathbf a)$.
drills.solution:
The chain rule multiplies outer times inner: $D(\mathbf G\circ\mathbf F)(\mathbf a) = D\mathbf G(\mathbf F(\mathbf a))\,D\mathbf F(\mathbf a)$.
Row 1: $({b11})({a11}) + ({b12})({a21}) = {c11}$ and $({b11})({a12}) + ({b12})({a22}) = {c12}$.
Row 2: $({b21})({a11}) + ({b22})({a21}) = {c21}$ and $({b21})({a12}) + ({b22})({a22}) = {c22}$.
**$\begin{bmatrix} {c11} & {c12}\\ {c21} & {c22}\end{bmatrix}$**. (Multiplying in the other order, $D\mathbf F\,D\mathbf G$, usually gives a different matrix.)

drills.title: Decay rate in the heat equation
drills.prompt: For which $\lambda$ does $u = e^{-\lambda t}\sin({n:coef}x)$ solve the heat equation $u_t = {al:coef}u_{xx}$? Then find the time at which the height of this profile has fallen to half its starting value (3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$u_t = -\lambda u$ and $u_{xx} = -{n2}u$, so $-\lambda = {al}\cdot(-{n2})$ and $\lambda =$ **{lam}**.
The height is $e^{-{lam}t}$. Setting $e^{-{lam}t} = \tfrac12$ gives $t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{{lam}} \approx$ **{th:sig3}**.

drills.title: Evaluate d'Alembert's solution
drills.prompt: A string obeys $u_{tt} = {c}^2u_{xx}$. It starts at rest ($u_t(x, 0) = 0$) with shape $u(x, 0) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$. Use d'Alembert's formula to find $u({x0}, {t0})$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution:
With $\psi = 0$, d'Alembert's formula is $u = \tfrac12\left[\varphi(x - ct) + \varphi(x + ct)\right]$ with $\varphi(s) = \dfrac{1}{1 + s^2}$.
Here $x - ct = {d1}$ and $x + ct = {d2}$, so $u = \tfrac12\left(\dfrac{1}{{q1}} + \dfrac{1}{{q2}}\right) = \dfrac{{num0}}{{den0}} =$ **$\dfrac{{num}}{{den}}$**.

drills.title: Classify by leading principal minors

calc.cls: if(D1 > 0 and D2 > 0 and D3 > 0, 1, if(D1 < 0 and D2 > 0 and D3 < 0, 2, 3))

drills.prompt: At a critical point of $f(x, y, z)$ the Hessian is $H = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {d} & 0\\ {d} & {b} & {e}\\ 0 & {e} & {c}\end{bmatrix}$. Find the leading principal minors $D_1$, $D_2$, $D_3$, then classify the point: type **1** for a local minimum, **2** for a local maximum, **3** for a saddle point.
drills.solution:
$D_1 = {a}$.
$D_2 = ({a})({b}) - ({d})^2 = {D2}$.
$D_3 = \det H = {a}\left(({b})({c}) - ({e})^2\right) - ({d})\left(({d})({c}) - 0\right) = {D3}$.
Signs $+, +, +$ mean a minimum; $-, +, -$ a maximum; any other pattern with $D_3 \ne 0$ a saddle. Here $D_1 = {D1}$, $D_2 = {D2}$, $D_3 = {D3}$: **type {cls}**.

drills.title: Critical point of a quadratic in three variables

calc.cls: if(D1 > 0 and D2 > 0 and D3 > 0, 1, if(D1 < 0 and D2 > 0 and D3 < 0, 2, 3))

drills.prompt: Find the critical point of $f(x, y, z) = {A:coef}x^2 {B:signedcoef}y^2 {C:signedcoef}z^2 {p:signedcoef}xy {q:signedcoef}yz {l1:signedcoef}x {l2:signedcoef}y {l3:signedcoef}z$, then classify it: type **1** for a local minimum, **2** for a local maximum, **3** for a saddle point.
drills.solution:
Set the gradient to zero:
$f_x = {A2:coef}x {p:signedcoef}y {l1:signed} = 0$, $f_y = {p:coef}x {B2:signedcoef}y {q:signedcoef}z {l2:signed} = 0$, $f_z = {q:coef}y {C2:signedcoef}z {l3:signed} = 0$.
Solving this linear system gives **$({X}, {Y}, {Z})$**. Check the first equation: ${A2}({X}) + ({p})({Y}) + ({l1}) = 0$.
The Hessian is constant: $H = \begin{bmatrix} {A2} & {p} & 0\\ {p} & {B2} & {q}\\ 0 & {q} & {C2}\end{bmatrix}$, with leading principal minors $D_1 = {D1}$, $D_2 = {D2}$, $D_3 = {D3}$.
$+, +, +$ is a minimum, $-, +, -$ a maximum, anything else (with $D_3 \ne 0$) a saddle: **type {cls}**.

drills.title: Maximize with an inequality constraint (KKT)
drills.prompt: Maximize $f(x, y) = -(x - {p})^2 - (y - {q})^2$ subject to ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y \le {k}$. Give the maximizing point and the KKT multiplier $\lambda$ (from $\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g$, with $\lambda = 0$ if the constraint is inactive). Exact fractions.
drills.solution:
Inactive case: $\nabla f = \mathbf 0$ at $({p}, {q})$, where ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {gpq}$. The limit is ${k}$, so this point is feasible exactly when ${gpq} \le {k}$.
Active case: $\nabla f = \langle -2(x - {p}), -2(y - {q})\rangle = \lambda\langle {a}, {b}\rangle$ gives $x = {p} - {ha:coef}\lambda$, $y = {q} - {hb:coef}\lambda$. Substituting into ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {k}$: ${gpq} - {hs:coef}\lambda = {k}$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{2({gpq} - {k})}{{ss}} = {lamA:texfrac}$, which must be $\ge 0$.
Exactly one case is valid here, giving $x =$ **${X:texfrac}$**, $y =$ **${Y:texfrac}$**, $\lambda =$ **${lam:texfrac}$**. ($f$ is concave and the constraint is linear, so this KKT point is the maximum: the point of the half-plane nearest $({p}, {q})$.)

drills.title: Two steps of gradient descent
drills.prompt: Apply two steps of gradient descent with step size $\alpha = {al}$ to $f(x, y) = {a:coef}(x {np:signed})^2 + {b:coef}(y {nq:signed})^2$, starting at $({x0}, {y0})$. Give the second iterate $(x_2, y_2)$ as exact decimals.
drills.solution:
$
abla f = \langle {a2}(x {np:signed}),\ {b2}(y {nq:signed})angle$, and each step is $\mathbf x_{n+1} = \mathbf x_n - {al}\,
abla f(\mathbf x_n)$.
Step 1: $
abla f({x0}, {y0}) = \langle {gx0}, {gy0}angle$, so $\mathbf x_1 = ({x0} - {al}({gx0}),\ {y0} - {al}({gy0})) = ({x1:num4}, {y1:num4})$.
Step 2: $
abla f(\mathbf x_1) = \langle {gx1:num4}, {gy1:num4}angle$, so $\mathbf x_2 =$ **$({x2:num4}, {y2:num4})$**.
(Shortcut: each step multiplies $x {np:signed}$ by $1 - 2({a})({al}) = {rx}$ and $y {nq:signed}$ by $1 - 2({b})({al}) = {ry}$.)

drills.title: One step of Newton's method
drills.prompt: Take one step of Newton's method for $f(x, y) = x^4 {c:signedcoef}y^2 {d:signedcoef}xy$ from the point $({x0}, {y0})$. Give the new point to 3 decimal places (or as exact fractions).
drills.solution:
$
abla f = \langle 4x^3 {d:signedcoef}y,\ {HC}y {d:signedcoef}xangle$ and $H =  egin{bmatrix} 12x^2 & {HB}\ {HB} & {HC}\end{bmatrix}$.
At $({x0}, {y0})$: $
abla f = \langle {g1}, {g2}angle$, $H =  egin{bmatrix} {HA} & {HB}\ {HB} & {HC}\end{bmatrix}$, $D = ({HA})({HC}) - ({HB})^2 = {DD}$.
$H^{-1}
abla f = \dfrac{1}{{DD}} egin{bmatrix} {HC} & {nHB}\ {nHB} & {HA}\end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix} {g1}\ {g2}\end{bmatrix} \approx \langle {s1:dp3}, {s2:dp3}angle$.
New point: $({x0}, {y0}) - H^{-1}
abla f \approx$ **$({x1:dp3}, {y1:dp3})$**.

drills.title: Midpoint rule and its error
drills.prompt: Use the midpoint rule with $2\times2$ equal sub-rectangles to estimate $\displaystyle\iint_R({pc:coef}x^2 + {qc:coef}y^2 {sc:signedcoef}xy)\,dA$ over $R = [0, {wid}]\times[0, {hgt}]$. Then find the error, exact value minus estimate. (Exact or 2 decimals.)

figure.caption: R = [0, {wid}] × [0, {hgt}] cut into four sub-rectangles, with their midpoints

drills.solution:
The midpoints are $x = {x1}, {x2}$ and $y = {y1}, {y2}$, and each sub-rectangle has area $\Delta A = {dA}$.
Adding $f$ at the four midpoints and multiplying by $\Delta A$ gives $M =$ **{mid:num4}** (about {mid:num2}).
Exactly, $\displaystyle\iint_R f\,dA = {pc}\cdot\frac{{wid}^3\cdot{hgt}}{3} + {qc}\cdot\frac{{wid}\cdot{hgt}^3}{3} + ({sc})\cdot\frac{{wid}^2\cdot{hgt}^2}{4} \approx {exact:num4}$.
The error is **{err:num4}** (about {err:num2}). Check with the error formula: the $xy$ term contributes no error (the midpoint rule is exact for it), and $\frac{h^2}{24}\iint f_{xx} + \frac{k^2}{24}\iint f_{yy}$ with $h = {wid}/2$, $k = {hgt}/2$ gives the same number, exactly, because $f$ is quadratic.

drills.title: Simpson's rule on one panel
drills.prompt: Use Simpson's rule with one panel (a $3\times3$ grid, $h = {hh}$, $k = {kk}$) to estimate $\displaystyle\iint_R e^{{cc}xy}\,dA$ over $R = [0, {wid}]\times[0, {hgt}]$. (4 decimals.)
drills.solution:
The grid is $x\in\{0, {hh}, {wid}\}$, $y\in\{0, {kk}, {hgt}\}$. Wherever $x = 0$ or $y = 0$ the integrand is $e^0 = 1$.
Corners (weight 1): $1 + 1 + 1 + e^{{uu}} \approx {e1:num4} + 3$. Edge midpoints (weight 4): $1 + 1 + 2e^{{uu}/2} \approx 2 + 2({e2:num4})$. Center (weight 16): $e^{{uu}/4} \approx {e4:num4}$.
The weighted sum is about {bracket:num4}, and $\dfrac{hk}{9} = \dfrac{{hh}\cdot{kk}}{9}$, so the estimate is **{est:num4}**.

drills.title: A Monte Carlo area estimate
drills.prompt: A region $D$ lies inside the rectangle $[0, {wid}]\times[0, {hgt}]$. Of {npts} points chosen uniformly at random in the rectangle, {hits} land in $D$. Estimate the area of $D$. Then: how many points would make the standard error about {fac} times smaller?
drills.solution:
The rectangle has area ${wid}\cdot{hgt} = {box}$, and the fraction of hits is ${hits}/{npts}$, so the area of $D$ is about ${box}\cdot\dfrac{{hits}}{{npts}} =$ **{est:num2}**.
The standard error shrinks like $1/\sqrt N$, so dividing it by {fac} needs ${fac}^2$ times as many points: ${npts}\cdot{fac}^2 =$ **{newn}**.

drills.title: An improper integral over a disk
drills.prompt: The integrand below blows up at the origin. Evaluate the improper integral $\displaystyle\iint_{x^2 + y^2\le {rad}^2}\frac{dA}{(x^2 + y^2)^{{qq}}}$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
In polar coordinates $(x^2 + y^2)^{{qq}} = r^{{rq}}$, and the exponent ${rq}$ is less than 2, so the integral converges. Exhaust the disk by rings $\varepsilon \le r \le {rad}$ and let $\varepsilon\to0$:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{{rad}}r^{-{rq}}\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\int_0^{{rad}}r^{{pw} - 1}\,dr = 2\pi\cdot\frac{{rad}^{{pw}}}{{pw}} \approx$ **{val:num2}**.

drills.title: Which waiting time ends first?
drills.prompt: $X$ and $Y$ are independent waiting times (in hours) with densities ${ra}e^{-{ra}x}$ for $x \ge 0$ and ${rb}e^{-{rb}y}$ for $y \ge 0$. Find $P(X < Y)$ as an exact fraction, and $P(X \le {tx},\ Y \le {ty})$ to 3 decimals.
drills.solution:
The joint density is $f(x, y) = {ra}\cdot{rb}\,e^{-{ra}x - {rb}y}$ on the first quadrant. It is nonnegative, so Tonelli's theorem lets us iterate the improper integrals.
$\displaystyle P(X < Y) = \int_0^\infty\int_x^\infty {ra}\cdot{rb}\,e^{-{ra}x - {rb}y}\,dy\,dx = \int_0^\infty {ra}\,e^{-{sumr}x}\,dx = \frac{{ra}}{{sumr}}$, so $P(X < Y) =$ **${pless:texfrac}$**.
The box probability factors because the density is a product: $\left(1 - e^{-{ra}\cdot{tx}}\right)\left(1 - e^{-{rb}\cdot{ty}}\right) \approx$ **{pbox:dp3}**.

drills.title: Moment of inertia of a standard solid

choices.label: a uniform solid ball, about a diameter
a uniform solid cylinder, about its axis
a thin uniform spherical shell, about a diameter
a thin uniform hoop, about its axis
a uniform solid cone, about its axis

drills.prompt: Find the moment of inertia of {k}, with mass {m} kg and radius {a} m. (kg·m², 3 significant figures.)
drills.solution:
For this shape $I = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}ma^2$ (from the table in the lesson).
$I = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}\cdot{m}\cdot{a}^2 \approx$ **{I:sig3}** kg·m².

drills.title: Parallel axis theorem
drills.prompt: A {k} has mass {m} kg and radius {a} m. Find its moment of inertia about an axis {d} m from its center, parallel to its central axis (for the ball, a diameter; for the cylinder, its own axis). (kg·m², 3 significant figures.)
drills.solution:
About the central axis, $I_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}ma^2 = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}\cdot{m}\cdot{a}^2 \approx {Icm:sig3}$.
Parallel axis theorem: $I = I_{\text{cm}} + md^2 \approx {Icm:sig3} + {m}\cdot{d}^2 \approx$ **{I:sig3}** kg·m².

drills.title: Speed after rolling down a ramp
drills.prompt: A {k} is released from rest and rolls without slipping down a ramp that drops {h} m. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its speed at the bottom. (m/s, 2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
For this shape $\beta = \dfrac{{num}}{{den}}$ in $I = \beta mR^2$. Energy: $mgh = \tfrac12(1 + \beta)mv^2$, so
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\cdot9.8\cdot{h}}{1 + {num}/{den}}} \approx$ **{v:num2}** m/s. (Mass and radius cancel.)

drills.title: Ellipsoid by a linear change of variables
drills.prompt: For the solid ellipsoid $\dfrac{x^2}{{a}^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{{b}^2} + \dfrac{z^2}{{c}^2} \le 1$, find its volume and $\displaystyle\iiint_E z^2\,dV$. (2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Use $x = {a}u$, $y = {b}v$, $z = {c}w$: the unit ball maps onto the ellipsoid and the Jacobian is ${a}\cdot{b}\cdot{c} = {abc}$.
$V = {abc}\cdot\tfrac43\pi \approx$ **{V:num2}**.
Over the unit ball $\iiint w^2\,dV = \tfrac13\iiint\rho^2\,dV = \tfrac{4\pi}{15}$, so $\iiint_E z^2\,dV = {abc}\cdot{c}^2\cdot\tfrac{4\pi}{15} \approx$ **{Z:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume between three pairs of parallel planes
drills.prompt: Find the volume of the solid $0 \le x {p:signedcoef}y \le {A}$, $0 \le y {q:signedcoef}z \le {B}$, $0 \le z {s:signedcoef}x \le {C}$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
Let $u = x {p:signedcoef}y$, $v = y {q:signedcoef}z$, $w = z {s:signedcoef}x$; the solid becomes a box of volume ${A}\cdot{B}\cdot{C} = {box}$.
$\dfrac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & {p} & 0\\ 0 & 1 & {q}\\ {s} & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 + ({p})({q})({s}) = {det}$, so $\left|\dfrac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}\right| = \dfrac{1}{|{det}|}$.
$V = \dfrac{{box}}{|{det}|} =$ **${V:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Volumes of revolution by Pappus
drills.prompt: A disk of radius {a}, centered {R} units from the $z$-axis in a half-plane through the axis, is revolved about the $z$-axis to make a torus. Find its volume. Then find the volume swept out by the square of side {side} with the same center. (2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Pappus: volume $= 2\pi\bar rA$, with $\bar r = {R}$ for both shapes (the centroid is the center).
Torus: $2\pi\cdot{R}\cdot\pi\cdot{a}^2 = 2\pi^2\cdot{R}\cdot{a}^2 \approx$ **{V:num2}**.
Square: $2\pi\cdot{R}\cdot{side}^2 \approx$ **{W:num2}**.

drills.title: Area of a polygon by the shoelace formula
drills.prompt: Use the shoelace formula to find the area of the quadrilateral with vertices $({X1}, {Y1})$, $({X2}, {Y2})$, $({X3}, {Y3})$, $({X4}, {Y4})$, listed counterclockwise.

figure.caption: The quadrilateral, vertices numbered in counterclockwise order

drills.solution:
For each edge, from $(x_i, y_i)$ to $(x_{i+1}, y_{i+1})$, compute $x_iy_{i+1} - x_{i+1}y_i$, wrapping around from the last vertex to the first:
$({X1})({Y2}) - ({X2})({Y1}) = {c1}$, $\;({X2})({Y3}) - ({X3})({Y2}) = {c2}$, $\;({X3})({Y4}) - ({X4})({Y3}) = {c3}$, $\;({X4})({Y1}) - ({X1})({Y4}) = {c4}$.
The sum is ${S}$, and half of it is the area: $A =$ **{A}**.

drills.title: Centroid of a polygon from its vertices
drills.prompt: Find the centroid $(\bar x, \bar y)$ of the quadrilateral with vertices $({X1}, {Y1})$, $({X2}, {Y2})$, $({X3}, {Y3})$, $({X4}, {Y4})$, listed counterclockwise. (2 decimal places.)
drills.solution:
Edge terms $c_i = x_iy_{i+1} - x_{i+1}y_i$: $c_1 = {c1}$, $c_2 = {c2}$, $c_3 = {c3}$, $c_4 = {c4}$, so $A = \tfrac12({c1} {c2:signed} {c3:signed} {c4:signed}) = {A}$ and $6A = {A6}$.
$\sum(x_i + x_{i+1})c_i = ({X1} {X2:signed})({c1}) + ({X2} {X3:signed})({c2}) + ({X3} {X4:signed})({c3}) + ({X4} {X1:signed})({c4}) = {Sx}$, so $\bar x = \dfrac{{Sx}}{{A6}} \approx$ **{xbar:num2}**.
$\sum(y_i + y_{i+1})c_i = ({Y1} {Y2:signed})({c1}) + ({Y2} {Y3:signed})({c2}) + ({Y3} {Y4:signed})({c3}) + ({Y4} {Y1:signed})({c4}) = {Sy}$, so $\bar y = \dfrac{{Sy}}{{A6}} \approx$ **{ybar:num2}**.

drills.title: Circulation from the winding number
drills.prompt: Let $\mathbf F = \left\langle\dfrac{{a:coef}x {mc:signedcoef}y}{x^2 + y^2},\; \dfrac{{a:coef}y {c:signedcoef}x}{x^2 + y^2}\right\rangle$. Evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$, where $C$ is the circle $(x {mh:signed})^2 + (y {mk:signed})^2 = {R2}$ traversed {n}, {dir}. (An exact answer such as 6pi is fine.)
drills.solution:
Split the field: $\mathbf F = {a}\,\nabla\!\left(\ln\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\right) + ({c})\,\mathbf V$, where $\mathbf V = \left\langle\frac{-y}{x^2 + y^2}, \frac{x}{x^2 + y^2}\right\rangle$ is the vortex field. The gradient part contributes 0 around any closed curve, and $\oint_C\mathbf V\cdot d\mathbf r = 2\pi w$, where $w$ is the winding number of $C$ around the origin.
The circle has center $({h}, {k})$ and radius ${R}$. The origin is inside exactly when $h^2 + k^2 < R^2$; here $h^2 + k^2 = {d2}$ and $R^2 = {R2}$. So $w = {w}$: from inside, the circle traversed {n} winds that many times around the origin, positive counterclockwise and negative clockwise; from outside it winds 0 times.
$\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r = 2\pi\cdot({c})\cdot({w}) =$ **${coefC}\pi \approx {ans:num2}$**.

drills.title: Divergence theorem on a cylinder, face by face
drills.prompt: Find the outward flux of $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}x,\; {b:coef}y,\; {c:coef}z^2\rangle$ through the closed surface of the solid cylinder $x^2 + y^2 \le {R}^2$, $0 \le z \le {H}$ (side, top and bottom). (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
By the Divergence theorem: $\operatorname{div}\mathbf F = {a} + {b} + 2({c})z$, and $\iiint_E\left({ab} + 2({c})z\right)dV$ gives the same total as the faces. Face by face, as in the proof:
Top ($z = {H}$, $\mathbf n = \mathbf k$): $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n = {c}\cdot{H}^2 = {cH2}$, times the area $\pi\cdot{R}^2$, gives $\approx {top:num2}$.
Bottom ($z = 0$, $\mathbf n = -\mathbf k$): $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n = 0$.
Side ($\mathbf n = \langle x, y, 0\rangle/{R}$): $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n = ({a}x^2 + {b}y^2)/{R}$; with $dS = {R}\,d\theta\,dz$ this integrates to $({a} + {b})\pi\cdot{R}^2\cdot{H} \approx {side:num2}$.
Total $\approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Stokes' theorem on a tilted plane
drills.prompt: Let $S$ be the part of the plane $z = {p:coef}x {q:signedcoef}y$ above the disk $x^2 + y^2 \le {R}^2$, oriented upward, and $\mathbf F = \langle y,\; z,\; x\rangle$. Find $\displaystyle\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r$ around its boundary, oriented by the right-hand rule. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F = \langle 0 - 1,\; 0 - 1,\; 0 - 1\rangle = \langle -1, -1, -1\rangle$. For the graph $z = g(x, y)$ with $g_x = {p}$, $g_y = {q}$, the upward normal is $\langle -g_x, -g_y, 1\rangle$, so
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf F\cdot\langle -g_x, -g_y, 1\rangle = ({p}) + ({q}) - 1 = {k}$.
By Stokes' theorem the circulation is ${k}\cdot\pi\cdot{R}^2 \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Flux out of a small cube
drills.prompt: For $\mathbf F = \langle {k:coef}x^3,\; 0,\; 0\rangle$, find the outward flux out of the cube of side {s} centered at $({x0}, 0, 0)$, and the limit of (flux)/(volume) as the side shrinks to 0 around the same center.
drills.solution:
Only the two faces $x = {x0} \pm \tfrac{{s}}{2}$ carry flux (on the others $\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n = 0$), each of area ${s}^2$.
Flux $= {k}\left[\left({x0} + \tfrac{{s}}{2}\right)^3 - \left({x0} - \tfrac{{s}}{2}\right)^3\right]\cdot{s}^2 =$ **{flux}**.
In general it is ${k}\left(3x_0^2h^3 + \tfrac{h^5}{4}\right)$ for side $h$; dividing by $h^3$ and letting $h\to0$ leaves $3({k})x_0^2 =$ **{lim}**, which is $\operatorname{div}\mathbf F$ at the center.

drills.title: Divergence by the product rule
drills.prompt: Use the product rule to find $\nabla\cdot(f\mathbf F)$ for $f = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}yz$ and $\mathbf F = \langle x,\; y,\; z\rangle$.
drills.solution:
$
abla f = \langle {a2:coef}x,\; {b:coef}z,\; {b:coef}yangle$, so $
abla f\cdot\mathbf F = {a2:coef}x^2 + ({b})yz + ({b})yz = {a2:coef}x^2 {b2:signedcoef}yz$.
$
abla\cdot\mathbf F = 3$, so $f\,
abla\cdot\mathbf F = {a3:coef}x^2 {b3:signedcoef}yz$.
Sum: **${a5:coef}x^2 {b5:signedcoef}yz$**.

drills.title: Flux of a gradient through a sphere
drills.prompt: Let $u = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}y^2 {c:signedcoef}z^2$. Find the outward flux of $\nabla u$ through the sphere $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = {R}^2$, that is, $\displaystyle\iint_S\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,dS$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
By Green's first identity with $u = 1$ (the Divergence theorem for $
abla u$), the flux is $\iiint_E
abla^2u\,dV$.
$
abla^2u = 2({a}) + 2({b}) + 2({c}) = {L}$, a constant, so the flux is ${L}\cdot	frac43\pi\cdot{R}^3 \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: Green's first identity for a linear function
drills.prompt: Let $u = {a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y {c:signedcoef}z$ and $S$ the sphere of radius {R} centered at the origin. Use Green's first identity to evaluate $\displaystyle\iint_S u\,\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,dS$. (2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Green's first identity with $v = u$: $\iint_S u\,\partial_nu\,dS = \iiint_E\left(u
abla^2u + |
abla u|^2ight)dV$.
$u$ is linear, so $
abla^2u = 0$ and $|
abla u|^2 = ({a})^2 + ({b})^2 + ({c})^2 = {G}$, a constant.
The value is ${G}\cdot	frac43\pi\cdot{R}^3 \approx$ **{ans:num2}**.

drills.title: A vector potential by Method 1
drills.prompt: The field $\mathbf F = \langle {a:coef}y^2,\; {b:coef}z,\; {c:coef}xy\rangle$ has divergence 0. Use Method 1 of the lesson ($A_3 = 0$, integrals starting from 0) to find $\mathbf A = \langle A_1, A_2, 0\rangle$ with $\nabla\times\mathbf A = \mathbf F$.
drills.solution:
Here $P = {a:coef}y^2$, $Q = {b:coef}z$, $R = {c:coef}xy$, so $R(x, s, 0) = {c:coef}xs$.
$A_2 = -\int_0^z P\,dt = -\int_0^z ({a:coef}y^2)\,dt = {ma:coef}y^2z$.
$A_1 = \int_0^z ({b:coef}t)\,dt - \int_0^y ({c:coef}xs)\,ds = {hb:coef}z^2 {mhc:signedcoef}xy^2$.
So $\mathbf A = \langle$ **${hb:coef}z^2 {mhc:signedcoef}xy^2$**, **${ma:coef}y^2z$**, $0\rangle$.
Check: $\nabla\times\mathbf A = \langle -\partial_zA_2,\; \partial_zA_1,\; \partial_xA_2 - \partial_yA_1\rangle = \langle {a:coef}y^2,\; {b:coef}z,\; 0 - ({mc:coef}xy)\rangle = \mathbf F$.

drills.title: Moving a vector potential to the Coulomb gauge
drills.prompt:
The vector potential $\mathbf A = \langle {p:coef}z^2,\; {a:coef}xy,\; {q:coef}xangle$ has $
abla\cdot\mathbf A = {a:coef}x$. Find $\chi = \chi(x)$, a function of $x$ alone with $\chi(0) = 0$ and $\chi'(0) = 0$, such that $\mathbf A + 
abla\chi$ is in the Coulomb gauge. Then give the first component of $\mathbf A + 
abla\chi$.
drills.solution:
We need $
abla^2\chi = -
abla\cdot\mathbf A = {k6:coef}x$, and for $\chi = \chi(x)$ that is $\chi'' ={k6:coef}x$.
Integrating twice with $\chi(0) = 0$ and $\chi'(0) = 0$: $\chi' = {k3:coef}x^2$ and $\chi =$ **${k:coef}x^3$**.
$
abla\chi = \langle {k3:coef}x^2, 0, 0angle$, so the first component becomes **${p:coef}z^2 {h:signedcoef}x^2$**. The curl is unchanged, and the new divergence is ${a:coef}x {k6:signedcoef}x = 0$.
